brief_extract:
CAROLINE HASLETT MEMORIAL TRUST
by MARY GEORGE, MBE, Companion IEE, Director EAW
THE Trust has just completed another successful year, successful not only from the point of view of the women it has helped with scholarships, bursaries and other awards but also because of the continued very generous support from its main contributors in the Electricity Supply Industry and from EAW branches. University scholarships
Donations from branches and from individuals amounted in 1968 to just under £800.

brief_context: Held a special minor scholarship at Edinburgh University.
brief_extract:
University scholarships
Donations from branches and from individuals amounted in 1968 to just under £800. This figure includes the regular annual contribution over the past four years from the Scottish branches to maintain the special minor scholarship held by Marion Lyall at Edinburgh University. One of the main calls on the Trust's funds is the annual major university scholarship which has been costing about £500 a year for the three years which the holder spends working for her degree in engineering, mathematics or one of the physical sciences.

associated_organisation: New Hall College, Cambridge; Central Electricity Generating Board
brief_context: A 1964 scholar who became a success story as a metallurgist.
brief_extract: How often our Selection Committee wishes we could give more than one scholarship particularly when we have some 30 or more candidates of very high calibre with outstanding school reports and examination achievements. A recent success story is that of Susan Thompson, our 1964 scholar, who was at New Hall College, Cambridge. She did so well in her third year tripos examination that her tutors recommended her to spend a fourth year at the university specialising in metallurgy.

associated_organisation: Radiation Limited; Central School of Arts and Crafts
brief_context: Won the first design bursary for household electrical equipment.
brief_extract: One can probably count on one finger of one hand the number of women actually engaged in designing household electrical equipment. So far as we know, Jennifer Cottis who won our first bursary for her designs for a matching plug and socket and a table standing electric cooker, is the only one of her kind. She has with our help obtained a job with Radiation Limited and we look forward in the not too distant future to seeing one of her brain children actually on the market.

The Biscuit Family
by MARJORIE PICKFORD

THE biscuit family has about as many ramifications as the Forsyte family and like most families it includes members who have changed their names but who still retain their family characteristics. Thus there are regional biscuits which may be called cakes such as the Goosnargh Cakes of Lancashire, and Dorset Knobs which are nearly identical with Norfolk Hollow biscuits.

JOAN Whitgift who died in the autumn was one of the women whose own career helped to lift the profession of home economist to the position which it occupies today. In her will just published she left a sum of money to mark achievement by women in the Electrical Industry.

title: Miss

A scheme is being worked out by her trustee, Miss Evelyn Gray, in consultation with the Director of the Electrical Association for Women in accordance with the terms of the will. The daughter of an electrical engineer, she was one of the industry's outstanding women and achieved many 'firsts'.

brief_context: Named in the trust that gave Joan Whitgift an award.
brief_extract: She was one of the first demonstrators to receive the EAW Diploma in Electrical Housecraft, and one of the earliest holders of the EDA Diploma in Public Speaking when she was working with the Brompton and Kensington Electricity Supply Company Ltd. In 1946 she was selected for the first award of a travelling exhibition made by the Caroline Haslett Trust and made an intensive tour of the Eastern United States studying many aspects of domestic electricity from the suppliers' and users' point of view. In view of the present focus of interest on home lighting it is note-worthy that Joan Whitgift made a study of home lighting techniques in two big American companies in Ohio and New Jersey.

title: Miss
brief_context: Mentioned statistics regarding women engineers in Russia.
brief_extract:
Our aim to increase our own standard of living would take us nowhere worth going to unless, at the same time, we sought to reduce the discrepancy between that of the developing countries of Africa, Asia, and South America and the one we ourselves already enjoyed. Women engineers
The lack of interest by girls in electrical engineering, and indeed in engineering generally, as a subject of university study in this country was referred to in a recent talk by Miss Rosina Winslade who mentioned that in Russia 1 in 3 professional engineers was a woman, whereas with us it was about 1 in 500. Our sociological concepts were, of course, very different from those in Russia, but this revealed what a pool of reserve ability we had to draw upon if we only knew how to do it, and not the least important aspect of this was how to improve the level of science teaching in girls’ schools.

F. Marsh, Deputy Chairman, Electricity Council; Lady De La Warr and Miss George

WE in the EAW were delighted when our national President, Lady De La Warr, who is also a member of the General Council of the British Electrical Approvals Board, was invited to open recently the new wing of the Electricity Council Appliance Testing Laboratories in Leatherhead. 21st Birthday of Testing House
These Laboratories were first established in London in 1948 by the then Electrical Development Association with the task of protecting the public by ensuring that the large number of electrical appliances coming on the market after the war were manufactured to proper standards of safety.
